key_insight: SARAH is the first real-time, fully causal method that makes conversational agents spatially aware—using a user's position and dyadic audio to generate natural, full‑body motion (turns, responses, gaze) suitable for streaming VR headsets.
problem_solved: Existing conversational-motion models ignore spatial context and/or require non-causal/offline processing, so agents fail to turn toward users, react to their movement, or maintain natural gaze in live VR/telepresence settings.
method: Causal, low-latency pipeline that runs in real time and is deployable on streaming VR hardware.
Conditions generation on user position (spatial cue) and dyadic audio to produce full-body motion and gaze that respond to the other participant.
Design and optimization choices focused on streaming/VR constraints (latency, continuous updates), enabling agentic, spatially-aware behavior.
impact: Enables VR, telepresence, and digital-human applications to exhibit natural, spatially-aware social behavior in live settings, improving immersion and social signaling while remaining practical to deploy on consumer streaming setups.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (headset position + dyadic audio) → SARAH model → avatar full-body motion & gaze output.
Before/After comparison: side-by-side avatars showing non-spatial vs spatially-aware reactions (turning, gaze tracking).
Real-time performance chart: latency and frame-rate under streaming conditions vs. baselines.
Iconic VR headset + skeleton overlay illustrating spatial cues (user position vector) and gaze direction.
paper_title: SARAH: Spatially Aware Real-time Agentic Humans
paper_authors: Evonne Ng, Siwei Zhang, Zhang Chen, Michael Zollhoefer, Alexander Richard
